concept: Degree of democracy (continuous or many-point scale)
how_to_choose: Prefer V-Dem when you need long coverage, separate democratic dimensions and measurement uncertainty; use Polity5 only for replication or pre-1900 comparison and note that it ends in 2018; use Freedom House when rights performance rather than institutions is the concept; UDS and SVMDI summarise several sources but are frozen; treat EIU, BTI and GSoD as assessments with shorter series and check their source overlap with V-Dem before using them as independent robustness checks.

concept: Democracy versus non-democracy; regime categories
how_to_choose: Binary codings disagree mainly on the participation threshold and on alternation rules. BMR requires both contestation and broad suffrage; DD/Bjørnskov-Rode require an alternation test; LIED offers a cumulative ordinal scale that nests several thresholds; RoW separates closed and electoral autocracies. Choose the rule that matches your theory and report results under at least one alternative coding.

concept: Type and inner workings of dictatorships
how_to_choose: GWF is the standard for regime-spell typologies and transitions (to 2010); Hadenius-Teorell-Wahman and va-PoReg offer typologies with later coverage; Svolik and Miller's ruling-party data add institutional detail; use the GWF latent personalism index when personalisation varies within a regime spell.

group: Episodes of regime change and backsliding
concept: Autocratization, democratization and incumbent power grabs
how_to_choose: ERT identifies episodes from changes in a V-Dem index, so it inherits V-Dem's scale; DEED and the incumbent-takeover data code discrete events from sources, which suits studies of mechanisms and sequencing. Use the event data to explain episodes defined by an index-based measure, not to re-measure the same thing.

concept: Broad governance quality
how_to_choose: WGI is the default cross-national governance measure but aggregates perception data, including commercial risk ratings such as ICRG, so it should not be used to validate those sources. Use CPIA only for IDA-eligible countries; IIAG for Africa; EQI for subnational Europe; SGI for OECD/EU members.

concept: Corruption (perceived, experienced or risk-based)
how_to_choose: Perception indices (CPI, BCI, WGI control of corruption) suit cross-national level comparisons; the CPI is only comparable over time from 2012. Experience surveys (GCB) and objective risk indicators from procurement records (GTI) capture different facets and are better for within-country change. BCI provides uncertainty estimates and longer harmonised series.

group: Rule of law and political constraints
concept: Constraints on rulers; rule of law
how_to_choose: POLCON derives constraints from the number of veto players and their partisan alignment; WJP measures rule of law from household and expert surveys for recent years only; DPI supplies the institutional inputs (checks, government fractionalisation) many constraint measures are built from.

concept: Administrative, extractive and informational capacity of the state
how_to_choose: Hanson-Sigman offers a latent cross-national measure (1960-2015) with uncertainty; O'Reilly-Murphy extends a capacity index back to 1789; the Information Capacity Dataset and Myers-score legibility data measure specific dimensions with objective indicators; RPC measures extraction relative to expected revenue; State Reach in Africa is geospatial. Match the dimension to the mechanism in your theory rather than using a general index.

concept: Fragility, instability and country risk
how_to_choose: FSI and the CSP State Fragility Index are open, but FSI combines outcome indicators (conflict, refugees) that are often dependent variables in political science. Commercial risk ratings (ICRG, PRS, EIU, BMI, S&P) are proprietary and forecast-oriented; ICRG's Researchers Dataset is the only one with a long academic track record.

concept: National election results (party/candidate votes and seats)
ids: ELEC-001; ELEC-002; ELEC-007; ELEC-029; ELEC-031; ELEC-036; ELEC-042; ELEC-038
how_to_choose: Use CLEA/THEA when you need constituency-level results across many countries; ParlGov for party-level national results in EU/OECD democracies linked to cabinets; IFES ElectionGuide for recent elections worldwide including non-democracies; Elections Global and the National Elections Database for long national series. Psephos and Election Passport are convenient but less documented.

concept: Electoral formula, district magnitude, thresholds, tiers
ids: ELEC-005; ELEC-004; ELEC-025; ELEC-026; ELEC-027; ELEC-028
how_to_choose: Bormann-Golder DES is the standard election-level source for democracies (1919-2020) with district magnitude and effective-number measures; IDEA's database gives current rules for all countries but little history; use Johnson-Wallack for personal-vote incentives and the Americas dataset for long Latin American series.

concept: Voter turnout (VAP vs registered voters)
how_to_choose: IDEA reports turnout against both registered voters and voting-age population; check which denominator a study uses because the two diverge sharply where registration is incomplete. GD-Turnout harmonises turnout across sources; EurLocalTurnout covers municipal elections; EAVS gives U.S. administrative counts.

concept: Freeness, fairness and manipulation of elections
ids: ELEC-009; ELEC-006; ELEC-011; ELEC-012; ELEC-013; ELEC-014; ELEC-016; ELEC-015; REG-001
how_to_choose: PEI measures expert perceptions of the whole electoral cycle since 2012 (note the 2023 series break); NELDA and QED code observable events and monitor reports back to 1945/1978; V-Dem's election indicators provide long annual series. Combine a perception-based and an event-based measure when integrity is the main variable.

concept: Results below the national level, linkable to geography
ids: ELEC-034; ELEC-035; ELEC-043; ELEC-045; ELEC-039; ELEC-040
how_to_choose: GRED provides constituency boundaries for CLEA results; EU-NED and BLUE_EP report results on NUTS regions and municipalities for Europe; SAGE offers small-area results globally; SEED/SLED cover subnational executive and legislative elections in Latin America.

concept: Federal, state and local returns in the United States
ids: ELEC-089; ELEC-090; ELEC-091; ELEC-093; ELEC-096; ELEC-104; ELEC-097; ELEC-092
how_to_choose: MEDSL is the default open source for federal returns since 1976 and precinct returns since 2016; VEST adds precinct boundaries; Leip's Atlas is the most complete county-level source but licensed; Klarner covers state legislative elections; ICPSR 1 and the Algara-Amlani county file serve historical work; Downballot re-tabulates presidential vote to districts.

concept: Electoral management, voting arrangements and franchise rules
ids: ELEC-017; ELEC-010; ELEC-105; ELEC-106; ELEC-018; ELEC-033
how_to_choose: IDEA EMD describes the formal model of electoral management bodies; the Electoral Management Survey measures their staff and practice; EAVS and the Elections Performance Index measure U.S. administration; IDEA Voting from Abroad and EVRR code external voting rights (EVRR has longer, systematically coded series).

concept: Referendums and initiatives
ids: ELEC-067; ELEC-068; ELEC-069; ELEC-070; ELEC-061; ELEC-071; ELEC-072
how_to_choose: Use the Referendum Database (c2d) for national votes worldwide, Swissvotes for Swiss federal votes, and NCSL or the Initiative & Referendum Institute for U.S. state measures; IDEA's database and the Navigator describe legal provisions rather than individual votes.

concept: U.S. district lines and redistricting plans
ids: ELEC-114; ELEC-115; ELEC-116; ELEC-117; ELEC-118; ELEC-119
how_to_choose: UCLA shapefiles give congressional boundaries since 1789; Carson-Crespin link districts over time; Wang-Cervas and the Redistricting Data Hub collect current plans; ALARM simulations provide neutral baselines for evaluating gerrymanders; P.L. 94-171 supplies the population counts.

concept: Left-right and issue positions of parties
ids: PARTY-001; PARTY-003; PARTY-005; PARTY-006; PARTY-007; PARTY-008; PARTY-036; PARTY-035; PARTY-076
how_to_choose: Manifesto data (MPDS) give election-by-election positions for programmes back to 1920 but measure emphasis rather than position; expert surveys (CHES, V-Party, Global Party Survey, POPPA) give direct placements but only at wave intervals and reflect party reputations. Use CHES for European issue dimensions, V-Party for global coverage and organisation, and validate main results with one measure from the other family. For parties before 1918, the Habsburg Manifesto Dataset (PARTY-076) codes Czech and German party appeals in Imperial Austria, 1897-1911.

concept: Which parties are populist, and how much
ids: PARTY-017; PARTY-007; PARTY-005; PARTY-021; PARTY-018; PARTY-020; PARTY-019
how_to_choose: The PopuList is the standard binary classification for Europe; POPPA and V-Party's anti-pluralism and populism indices provide continuous expert scores; the Global Populism Database scores leaders' speeches rather than parties. Binary lists suit counts and party-family studies; continuous scores suit degree-of-populism questions.

concept: Formal rules, members, resources and linkage strategies
ids: PARTY-010; PARTY-011; PARTY-012; PARTY-014; PARTY-013; PARTY-016
how_to_choose: PPDB codes statutes and resources across about 50 democracies; DALP measures clientelistic and programmatic linkage from expert surveys; MAPP gives membership series; IPOD integrates several organisation datasets. Formal rules (PPDB) and practice (DALP) can diverge, so choose by whether the theory concerns rules or behaviour.

concept: Volatility, new parties, fragmentation and instability
ids: PARTY-023; PARTY-025; PARTY-026; PARTY-024; PARTY-028; PARTY-027; PARTY-051; PARTY-052
how_to_choose: The CISE datasets decompose volatility into regeneration and alteration components for Western Europe; Mainwaring-Su cover Latin America; net volatility (Dassonneville) suits voter-level comparisons. Volatility measures are sensitive to how splits and mergers are coded, so pair them with the Ibenskas splits-and-mergers data where party continuity matters.

concept: Pre-CHES party placements
ids: PARTY-029; PARTY-030; PARTY-031; PARTY-008; PARTY-061; PARTY-033; PARTY-032
how_to_choose: These surveys are frozen and use different scales and party lists; link them through Party Facts and rescale before comparing with CHES or V-Party. Use them for long-run comparison and replication, not for current positions.

group: Group appeals and issue emphasis from text
concept: Which groups and issues parties address
ids: PARTY-038; PARTY-039; PARTY-040; PARTY-041; PARTY-073; PARTY-054
how_to_choose: These datasets code party documents (manifestos, press releases) for social-group appeals, immigration positions or nostalgia; they are narrower than the MPDS but measure concepts the MPDS categories do not capture directly.

group: Legislator ideal points from roll calls
concept: Legislators' revealed preferences
how_to_choose: Voteview's DW-NOMINATE is the standard for the U.S. Congress; Shor-McCarty bridges state legislatures through candidate surveys; the Hix-Noury-Roland data (to 2009) and HowTheyVote.eu (since 2019) cover the European Parliament; BTVote and the Dutch voting dataset cover national parliaments. All roll-call-based scores share a selection problem where recorded votes are a non-random subset of decisions. For Canada since Confederation, Godbout and Hoyland's Lost on Division divisions (LEG-093, House and Senate) are the open roll-call source; the deposited files end in 2011.

concept: Who legislators are and how careers unfold
how_to_choose: Use congress-legislators or Bioguide for the U.S.; the Comparative Legislators Database for 16 countries with Wikipedia-linked identifiers; the Global Legislators Database and WARP for broad cross-national snapshots; LALD for Latin America. Completeness in Wikipedia-based datasets is uneven for older and less prominent members.

concept: Bills, laws and their significance
how_to_choose: The Congressional Bills Project and Libgober's federal laws data give bill- and law-level records; LES summarises member effectiveness; Mayhew and Clinton-Lapinski identify important laws; Open States and LegiScan cover state bills; the Toshkov and CEPS EurLex datasets cover EU legislative output.

concept: What legislators say on the floor
how_to_choose: ParlSpeech offers comparable full-text debates for nine democracies to about 2019; parliamentary-question datasets cover oversight activity in single countries. For text beyond 2019 use national open-data portals or the TEXT-domain corpora.

concept: Powers, rules and organisation of parliaments
how_to_choose: IPU Parline is the global reference for chamber structure and membership but overwrites past values for non-time-series fields; ParlRulesData codes procedural rules over time; the Squire index measures U.S. state legislative professionalism; the Deployment Votes Database covers parliamentary war powers.

concept: Primary machine-readable records from parliaments
how_to_choose: National portals are current and authoritative but differ in coverage start dates, identifiers and licences; academic datasets built on them add cleaning and stable IDs. Record the API version and access date.

concept: Who held executive office, when, and how they entered and left
ids: EXEC-002; EXEC-003; EXEC-008; EXEC-006; EXEC-009; EXEC-039; EXEC-015
how_to_choose: Archigos is the standard leader-spell dataset (1875-2015) with entry and exit modes; REIGN extends monthly coverage to 2021; the post-1789 leader-survival file and WorldStatesmen/Zárate give longer historical lists. CHISOLS records changes in the leader's support coalition rather than leader turnover alone; choose it when the theory concerns shifts in the ruling coalition.

concept: Background, experience, ideology and party of leaders
ids: EXEC-005; EXEC-007; EXEC-010; EXEC-011; EXEC-012; EXEC-013; EXEC-014; EXEC-043
how_to_choose: LEAD and PolEx describe leaders' prior experience; Herre's Global Leader Ideology and Brambor-Lindvall code economic ideology, while Leaders Global records party affiliation linked to Party Facts. Merge on Archigos leader IDs where provided and check coverage end dates, which range from 2004 to 2023.

concept: Composition of governments below the head of government
ids: EXEC-004; EXEC-017; EXEC-019; EXEC-018; EXEC-020; EXEC-021; EXEC-022; ELEC-002
how_to_choose: WhoGov is the broadest minister-level source (1966-2025, global); Seki-Williams covers parliamentary democracies' governments to 2014; ParlGov (ELEC-002) links European cabinets to parties; Paths to Power adds social backgrounds. Choose by country scope and by whether individual ministers or whole cabinets are the unit.

concept: Formation, type, duration and termination of governments
ids: EXEC-001; EXEC-024; EXEC-025; EXEC-026; EXEC-027; EXEC-023
how_to_choose: REPDEM/Party Government in Europe and ParlGov are the core sources for European coalition research; PSGo extends coverage to 1848; the Parliamentary Events Dataset separates full-power from caretaker cabinets; the Ganghof data code support arrangements for minority governments. Coding rules for when a new cabinet begins differ across sources and drive duration estimates.

concept: Constitutional and practical limits on executives
how_to_choose: Doyle-Elgie scores aggregate several published presidential-power measures; Borges codes presidential powers and regime type; AETL and the Versteeg et al. evasion data record term-limit rules and attempts to circumvent them. Pair with constitutional data (CONST) when formal rules are the focus.

concept: What constitutions say
ids: CONST-001; CONST-002; CONST-003; CONST-004; CONST-005; CONST-006
how_to_choose: The Comparative Constitutions Project is the standard coded source for constitutional content and change since 1789; Constitute gives searchable texts of current constitutions; WORLD, Academic Freedom in Constitutions and the UN Women database code specific rights. All measure de jure provisions; pair them with the Comparative Constitutional Compliance Database or V-Dem indicators when practice matters.

concept: Inclusive, dispersive and constraining institutions; emergency rule
ids: CONST-008; CONST-009; CONST-010; CONST-011; CONST-012; CONST-013; CONST-026
how_to_choose: IDC is the main cross-national power-sharing dataset (1975-2019) and IAEP covers a wider set of formal institutions to 2012; the Constitutional Power-Sharing Dataset extends coverage of constitutional provisions; Lijphart's data define the classic consensus-majoritarian patterns for 36 democracies. Emergency-power datasets differ in whether they code constitutional provisions or actual declarations.

concept: Regional authority, local autonomy and fiscal decentralization
ids: CONST-015; CONST-016; CONST-017; CONST-021; CONST-022; CONST-023; CONST-024; CONST-025; CONST-031; CONST-032
how_to_choose: The Regional Authority Index measures self-rule and shared rule of regional governments (1950-2018) and the Local Autonomy Index does the same for municipalities in Europe (1990-2020); IMF, OECD and SNG-WOFI report fiscal decentralization from public-finance statistics. Institutional indices and fiscal ratios capture different concepts and often diverge (Harguindéguy, Cole and Pasquier 2021); choose by whether authority or resources is the quantity of interest.

group: U.S. Supreme Court decisions and judicial ideology
concept: Votes, decisions and justices' preferences
ids: CONST-035; CONST-036; CONST-037; CONST-038; CONST-039; CONST-047
how_to_choose: The Supreme Court Database is the reference record of decisions and votes; Martin-Quinn scores give vote-based dynamic ideal points, Segal-Cover scores give pre-confirmation newspaper-based ideology, and the Judicial Common Space and Bonica-Sen place judges on a scale shared with other actors. Avoid using vote-based scores to explain the same votes (Fischman and Law 2008).

concept: De jure and de facto independence of courts
ids: CONST-076; CONST-077; CONST-078; CONST-079; CONST-080; CONST-081; CONST-082; CONST-083
how_to_choose: Linzer-Staton's latent judicial independence pools many indicators into a single score with uncertainty; Feld-Voigt separate de jure and de facto independence; La Porta et al. code constitutional judicial checks for a single period. Existing measures agree only weakly with one another (Ríos-Figueroa and Staton 2012), so robustness across at least two measures is advisable.

concept: Weberianness, impartiality, professionalization and effectiveness of public administration
how_to_choose: The QoG Expert Survey measures bureaucratic structure (professionalization, impartiality, closedness) from public-administration experts; Evans-Rauch is the historical Weberianness benchmark for 35 developing countries; the Blavatnik Index (successor of InCiSE) scores civil-service effectiveness for about 120 countries. V-Dem's public-administration indicators and WGI government effectiveness give longer annual series but mix bureaucratic quality with broader governance.

concept: Size, composition and attitudes of the public workforce
how_to_choose: WWBI and ILOSTAT give cross-national public-employment and wage measures from household and labour-force surveys; the Global Survey of Public Servants measures attitudes and management practices inside administrations; FEVS, OPM Federal Workforce Data and ASPEP cover the U.S. federal, state and local workforce. Survey-based employment counts and administrative headcounts differ in what they count as public employment.

concept: Formal design, independence and politicization of agencies
how_to_choose: GlobalReg and the regulatory-agency diffusion data cover agencies cross-nationally; Selin's independence scores, the ACUS Sourcebook, Lewis's insulation and appointee data and Bednar's capacity scores cover U.S. federal agencies in depth. Formal independence and political control in practice should be distinguished; the U.S. datasets allow both.

group: Public financial management and digital government
concept: Budget processes, transparency and digital services
how_to_choose: PEFA assesses public financial management systems against a common framework, the Open Budget Survey measures budget transparency and oversight biennially, and BOOST provides spending microdata; EGDI, the OECD Digital Government Index and the GovTech Maturity Index measure digital government with different country coverage and emphasis (services vs. institutional readiness).

concept: Which issues governments and parties attend to
ids: POLICY-001; POLICY-002; POLICY-003; POLICY-004; POLICY-005; POLICY-006; LEG-002
how_to_choose: The Comparative Agendas Project codes bills, hearings, speeches, budgets and media by a common major-topic scheme across about 20 countries; the U.S. Policy Agendas Project is its longest series; ParlaCAP machine-codes parliamentary speeches. These measure attention, not policy direction; use pledge data (POLICY-006) or position data when the content of policy matters.

concept: Policy adoption, innovation and ideology across U.S. states
ids: POLICY-008; POLICY-009; POLICY-010; POLICY-011; POLICY-012; POLICY-013; POLICY-014; POLICY-015
how_to_choose: SPID records first adoptions of 724 policies to 2017 and is the standard diffusion dataset; CSPP merges over 3,000 state-year variables; Caughey-Warshaw (to 2014) and Grumbach (1970-2014) measure overall policy liberalism from different policy sets, so results can depend on the choice. Text-as-Policy and the Garlick bill data capture legislative activity below adoption.

concept: Organised interests, lobbying activity and positions
ids: POLICY-020; POLICY-021; POLICY-022; POLICY-023; POLICY-024; POLICY-025; POLICY-026; POLICY-027
how_to_choose: The Washington Representatives Study and the Comparative Interest Group Survey map group populations; LobbyView links U.S. lobbying reports to bills and firms; IGscores and MapLight record groups' bill positions; LobbyFacts covers EU Transparency Register data. Disclosure-based data capture registered lobbying only.

concept: Benefit generosity, social protection and pensions
ids: POLICY-032; POLICY-033; POLICY-034; POLICY-035; POLICY-038; POLICY-039; POLICY-041; POLICY-042; POLICY-043; POLICY-044
how_to_choose: SPIN and TaxBEN measure legislated entitlements for model households in rich democracies; the ILO World Social Protection Database, ASPIRE and SALMIC cover coverage and programmes in middle- and low-income countries from administrative and survey data. Entitlement and spending measures (OECD SOCX, catalogued under PE) answer different questions about welfare effort.

group: Labour market regulation and minimum wages
concept: Employment protection and wage-floor institutions
ids: POLICY-052; POLICY-053; POLICY-054; POLICY-055; POLICY-056; POLICY-057; POLICY-058; POLICY-059; POLICY-060
how_to_choose: OECD EPL indicators are the standard for OECD countries; the CBR Labour Regulation Index covers a wider set of countries and a longer period with documented coding; ILO EPLex gives legal detail. For minimum wages, OECD data give levels relative to median wages, while WageIndicator and the Tijdens database record setting institutions.

concept: Government responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, 2020-2022
ids: POLICY-064; POLICY-065; POLICY-066; POLICY-067; POLICY-068; POLICY-069
how_to_choose: OxCGRT provides ordinal indicators and composite indices for 185 countries and many subnational units; CoronaNet codes individual policy events in more detail; HIT-COVID and the ECDC-JRC database add subnational and European coverage. Indices built from different coding schemes are not interchangeable (Shen et al.).

concept: Values, social attitudes and political orientations across countries
ids: OPIN-002; OPIN-003; OPIN-004; OPIN-038; OPIN-005; OPIN-006; OPIN-019
how_to_choose: WVS and EVS give the longest and broadest coverage of values (1981-2023) but with uneven country participation; the ESS offers the strongest sampling and translation standards for Europe; ISSP fields rotating topical modules; the Gallup World Poll is annual and global but commercial. Use the Integrated Values Surveys file for long trends and the ESS for European comparisons where survey quality matters most.

concept: Democratic attitudes and governance evaluations by world region
ids: OPIN-010; OPIN-011; OPIN-012; OPIN-013; OPIN-014; OPIN-015; OPIN-017; OPIN-008
how_to_choose: The Global Barometer family (Afrobarometer, Arab, Asian, AmericasBarometer, Latinobarómetro) share core democracy items but differ in question wording, timing and sampling, so pooled analyses need harmonisation (see SDR2, Claassen's latent mood). Eurobarometer is frequent but designed for EU policy monitoring; Pew Global Attitudes covers fewer countries with consistent items.

concept: Vote choice and electoral behaviour
ids: OPIN-007; OPIN-009; OPIN-099; OPIN-101; OPIN-045; OPIN-052; OPIN-062; OPIN-083; OPIN-085; OPIN-020
how_to_choose: National election studies are the richest sources for each country; CSES harmonises a common module across them for comparative work (59 polities in the IMD); the European Election Studies cover European Parliament elections. In the U.S., ANES offers probability samples since 1948 while the Cooperative Election Study offers very large opt-in samples suited to state and small-group analysis.

concept: Macro-level opinion series built from many surveys
ids: OPIN-035; OPIN-036; OPIN-039; OPIN-040; OPIN-115; OPIN-116; OPIN-117; OPIN-118; OPIN-119; OPIN-136
how_to_choose: These measures pool many surveys into country-year or state-year series (democratic support, policy mood, macropartisanship, subnational ideology). They depend on the input surveys and on model assumptions; check sensitivity to the estimation method, as debated for latent democratic support (Claassen vs. Tai-Hu-Solt).

concept: Public approval of presidents and governors
how_to_choose: Gallup's presidential approval series ran from 1937 until it ended at the start of 2026; Roper's multi-pollster archive and the State Executive Approval Database (governors) extend coverage. Combine pollsters only with house-effect corrections.

concept: Output, income and growth across countries and over time
how_to_choose: Use WDI or the IMF WEO for current-dollar and constant-price series from 1960 or 1980 onward. Use PWT when cross-country comparisons of real output and productivity at purchasing power parity matter, and the Maddison Project for long-run GDP per capita before 1950. The Global Macro Database and JST harmonise many sources into long panels. All of these series are revised between releases, so cite the version and do not mix vintages.

concept: Gini coefficients, top income shares and distributions
how_to_choose: SWIID maximises comparable coverage through imputation and supplies uncertainty that should be carried into analyses. WID focuses on top shares built from tax data and national accounts. LIS offers harmonised microdata for richer countries. WIID and PIP compile survey-based estimates with documented welfare concepts. Do not combine Gini values computed on income and on consumption, or before and after taxes and transfers.

concept: Tax revenue and its composition
how_to_choose: The UNU-WIDER GRD (frozen in 2025) and its successor, the IMF World Revenue Longitudinal Database, cover developing countries from 1980. OECD Global Revenue Statistics has the most consistent tax classification but fewer countries. IMF GFS adds expenditure by function. Financing the State and the Comparative Income Taxation Database extend coverage back to the nineteenth century. Check whether social contributions and resource revenues are included before comparing series.

concept: Government debt and the timing of banking, currency and debt crises
how_to_choose: IMF Public Finances in Modern History and the Global Debt Database are maintained and are the broadest sources on government debt; the Historical Public Debt Database and Jaimovich-Panizza are frozen. Crisis dates differ by definition: Laeven-Valencia codes systemic banking crises from policy responses, while Reinhart-Rogoff and JST rely on narrative and historical criteria. Use World Bank International Debt Statistics for the external debt of developing economies.

concept: De jure restrictions on cross-border capital flows
how_to_choose: Chinn-Ito KAOPEN has the widest coverage but summarises binary AREAER categories and is re-estimated with each release. Fernandez et al. separate inflow and outflow controls by asset class, and the Quinn measure codes intensity. Rector-Kastner records the timing of policy changes for an earlier period. Findings on liberalisation are sensitive to the measure chosen (Karcher and Steinberg 2013), so check robustness across measures.

concept: Legal independence of central banks
how_to_choose: Garriga and the Romelli CBIE extend the Cukierman-Webb-Neyapti coding of central bank laws to most countries and recent decades; CBIE adds dimensions and reaches back to the 1920s for some banks. Governor turnover (Dreher-Sturm-de Haan) is a behavioural proxy for de facto independence. Legal and de facto measures diverge in many developing countries, so state which concept is meant.

concept: Market-oriented institutions and regulatory burden
how_to_choose: The Fraser and Heritage indices aggregate many indicators into composite scores that reflect their producers' definitions of economic freedom; use components rather than headline scores when a specific institution is of interest. OECD PMR measures product-market regulation for OECD and partner countries. Doing Business ended in 2021 and is not comparable with its successor, B-READY.

concept: Social spending and benefit generosity in rich democracies
how_to_choose: Spending data (SOCX, also carried in CPDS and the Comparative Welfare States dataset) reflect both policy and need. Entitlement data (CWED, SPIN) code what programmes promise to model households. Use spending for fiscal effort and entitlements for generosity; all of these cover mainly OECD countries.

concept: Merchandise trade between countries
how_to_choose: UN Comtrade is the primary customs-based source. CEPII BACI reconciles importer and exporter reports at product level and is usually preferable for research. IMF IMTS (formerly DOTS) gives aggregate bilateral totals. For trade before 1938 use Federico-Tena. CEPII Gravity adds distance, language and agreement variables for gravity models.

concept: Tariffs, non-tariff measures and industrial policy
how_to_choose: Applied and bound tariffs come from WTO TTD, WITS/TRAINS or the Teti Global Tariff Database, which fills gaps in the official sources. Global Trade Alert and NIPO record discrete policy interventions since 2008-2009, and the Temporary Trade Barriers Database covers anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard actions. Intervention counts reflect the monitors' search effort and are not measures of how restrictive policy is.

concept: Composite measures of economic, social and political integration
how_to_choose: The KOF Globalisation Index separates de facto from de jure and economic from social and political dimensions, and is the usual choice for country-year panels from 1970. The DHL index measures the depth and breadth of flows for recent years. The IPE Data Resource compiles many underlying variables for building custom measures.

concept: Oil, gas and mineral production, rents and governance
how_to_choose: Ross-Mahdavi (to 2014) gives oil and gas production and value per capita; Haber-Menaldo provides long-run fiscal reliance on resources from 1800. Sector governance is covered by the Resource Governance Index (superseded) and the National Oil Company Database, and EITI reports give government receipts. Production-based and revenue-based measures capture different concepts of dependence.

concept: Human development, poverty and wellbeing indices
how_to_choose: The HDI and its historical (AHDI) and subnational (SHDI) versions combine income, health and education. The Global MPI measures overlapping deprivations from household surveys. Think-tank and commercial composites (Social Progress, Legatum) use weightings chosen by their producers. Prefer component indicators to composite scores in causal analysis.

concept: Loans and development finance from Chinese state lenders
how_to_choose: Horn-Reinhart-Trebesch reconstruct loans and hidden debts from 1949; the Boston University database covers commitments by the two Chinese policy banks from 2008; the Chinese Loans to Africa database is Africa-specific. AidData's Global Chinese Development Finance dataset (to be catalogued under IR) is broader. Totals differ across sources because of coverage rules and tracking methods.

concept: Threats, displays and uses of force between states
how_to_choose: COW MID is the standard dispute-level and dyadic source; MIC (the ICDP successor to the GML corrections) recodes many MID cases, and studies that rely on dispute onsets should test both. MIE records individual militarized events and suits analyses of escalation within disputes. ICB measures crises from the perspective of decision makers and includes crises without militarized action; ICBe extracts event sequences from ICB narratives. Choose by unit: dispute, event or crisis.

concept: Wars and conquest attempts between states
how_to_choose: COW Inter-State War data remain the reference list. Reiter-Stam-Horowitz revise COW war participation and outcomes and extend coverage to 2019; the Modern Conquest dataset records attempts to seize territory, many of which fall below war thresholds. Report robustness to the war list used, because participant and outcome coding differ.

concept: Formal alliances and defence cooperation
how_to_choose: ATOP codes the specific obligations in alliance treaties and is more current than COW Formal Alliances, which records alliance type only. Defence cooperation agreements (DCAD) and joint military exercises capture cooperation short of alliance. Use ATOP when obligations matter and COW alliances for long-run comparisons with older work.

concept: Material power and defence spending
how_to_choose: COW NMC (CINC) offers the longest series but measures crude aggregates. SIPRI Military Expenditure is the reference for spending since 1949, and the Global Military Spending Dataset reconciles several sources back to 1816 with uncertainty estimates. IISS Military Balance gives force structure and equipment (licensed). rDMC and Power at Sea measure specific capabilities. Prefer measures matched to the type of power the theory concerns.

concept: International transfers of major and small arms
how_to_choose: The SIPRI Arms Transfers Database covers major conventional weapons since 1950 using a volume measure (trend-indicator values) that is not a financial value. UNROCA relies on state self-reports, with gaps. NISAT (small arms, frozen) and Bruegel's U.S. Foreign Military Sales data cover narrower flows. Do not compare SIPRI TIVs with sales values.

concept: Lists of independent states and system membership
how_to_choose: COW State System and Gleditsch-Ward differ in entry and exit dates and in the treatment of some states; ISD extends coverage beyond Europe-centred definitions in the nineteenth century. Use the list that matches the other datasets being merged, and use the states or peacesciencer packages to build panels consistently.

concept: Contested territory and enduring rivalry
how_to_choose: ICOW codes territorial, river and maritime claims with their salience; COW Territorial Change records completed transfers. Strategic rivalries (Thompson) rely on perceptions of threat, while Klein-Goertz-Diehl rivalries and the Peace Data derive from dispute patterns. Rivalry lists overlap only partly, so state the definition used.

concept: Threats and impositions of economic sanctions
how_to_choose: The Global Sanctions Data Base has the widest and most current coverage of imposed sanctions; TIES includes threats as well as impositions (to 2005); HSE gives detailed case studies with success scores. EUSANCT, the Targeted Sanctions Consortium and SPITS focus on EU and UN sanctions. Results on effectiveness depend on whether threats are included, so pick TIES when anticipation effects matter.

concept: IGO membership, informal IOs and delegated authority
how_to_choose: COW IGO provides membership panels to 2014; the Yearbook of International Organizations is broader but licensed. IIGO and Roger-Rowan cover informal bodies. MIA and the International Authority Database measure how much authority states delegate or pool, with different coding schemes; TRANSACCESS measures openness to non-state actors.

concept: Alignment of states in UN votes and other behaviour
how_to_choose: UNGA ideal points (Bailey-Strezhnev-Voeten) are the standard measure of foreign-policy preferences and correct for changes in the agenda; raw votes now come from UNGA-DM. Pardee's coincidence data add Security Council and Human Rights Council votes. FPSIM provides chance-corrected similarity scores from alliances and votes; S-scores and Gartzke's Affinity are older alternatives.

concept: Embassies, ambassadors and diplomatic networks
how_to_choose: COW Diplomatic Exchange (to 2005) is superseded for recent years by the Diplometrics data (1960-2025). The Lowy Global Diplomacy Index counts posts of selected countries in recent editions; GenDip adds the gender of ambassadors; DipRep extends coverage into the nineteenth century.

concept: Official development finance by donor, recipient and project
how_to_choose: OECD CRS is the reference for DAC donors' project-level aid; IATI offers more timely activity reports from a wider set of publishers. AidData's research releases add geocoding and non-DAC donors, and its Global Chinese Development Finance dataset tracks Chinese finance not reported to the OECD. Distinguish commitments from disbursements and grants from loans before combining sources.

concept: Content and depth of preferential trade agreements
how_to_choose: DESTA codes the design and depth of agreements since 1945; the World Bank Deep Trade Agreements data code policy areas and provisions in detail; the WTO RTA database is the official list of notified agreements. LABPTA and TRADEM specialise in labour and democracy provisions. Depth indices built from different codebooks are not interchangeable.

concept: Foreign military interventions and regime change
how_to_choose: IMI (1946-2005) and IMIC (1992-2022) record troop interventions across states; MIP focuses on U.S. interventions over a long period; FIRC codes foreign-imposed regime change; HMI covers humanitarian interventions. PEIG records covert and overt electoral interventions by great powers. Definitions of intervention differ, so the choice determines the sample.

concept: Peace operations and their mandates and contributors
how_to_choose: The IPI database recorded monthly troop and police contributions to UN missions for 1990-2018 and is now discontinued (archived copies only); SIPRI's Multilateral Peace Operations database covers non-UN operations as well (currently offline while moving to monthly data); PEMA codes mandate tasks; UNCR/UNPR code Security Council resolutions on conflicts and peacekeeping.

concept: State-linked cyber incidents
how_to_choose: DCID codes dyadic incidents between rival states with severity scores (to 2020); the CFR tracker and EuRepoC are broader, continuously updated incident collections. Attribution is uncertain in all three, and coverage depends on public reporting.

group: Lists of civil wars and armed conflicts
concept: Which internal conflicts occurred and when
ids: CONF-001; CONF-025; CONF-028; CONF-029; CONF-027; CONF-098; CONF-100; CONF-024
how_to_choose: UCDP/PRIO uses a low threshold (25 battle deaths per year) and is updated annually; COW, Fearon-Laitin and Sambanis use war-level thresholds (about 1,000 deaths) and differ in onset and termination rules. PITF and MEPV add magnitude scores. Results on civil war onset are known to be sensitive to the list chosen, so report robustness across at least two.

concept: Battle-related and civilian fatalities
how_to_choose: UCDP Battle-Related Deaths and the GED provide annual and event-level counts since 1989 with low, best and high estimates; the PRIO Battle Deaths data extend back to 1946 but stop in 2008. The Global Violent Deaths database combines conflict and non-conflict violence; Iraq Body Count is a case-specific record. Use the uncertainty bounds, since estimates for intense wars differ widely.

concept: Where and when violent events happened
how_to_choose: UCDP GED codes fatal events in organized violence with conservative inclusion rules; ACLED codes a broader set of political violence and protest events, including non-fatal ones, and is updated weekly but requires registration. xSub harmonises many subnational sources to common units (frozen at 2019; served through a temporary app). Coverage and inclusion rules differ, so counts are not interchangeable.

concept: Automated coding of political events from news
ids: CONF-033; CONF-034; CONF-035; CONF-036; CONF-037; CONF-038
how_to_choose: GDELT is the largest and most current source but has substantial duplication and false positives; ICEWS (to 2023) and its successor POLECAT apply curated dictionaries and are more precise; the Cline Center Phoenix data extend back to 1945 using archival news. Validate event counts against hand-coded data for the cases studied.

concept: Terrorist attacks and their attributes
ids: CONF-069; CONF-070; CONF-071; CONF-072; CONF-073; CONF-074
how_to_choose: The Global Terrorism Database is the broadest incident list (1970-2020, now frozen) and includes domestic attacks; RAND (to 2009) and ITERATE (commercial) focus on transnational terrorism; CPOST covers suicide attacks; TWEED and RTV cover Western Europe. Definitions and source coverage differ, especially before 1998 and for domestic events.

concept: Attempted and successful coups
ids: CONF-084; CONF-085; CONF-086; CONF-087; CONF-088; EXEC-003
how_to_choose: Powell-Thyne is the standard list of coup attempts and is updated continuously; the Cline Center and Colpus datasets use broader or more detailed definitions and add coup agents and types; REIGN records coups within a monthly leader panel. Definitions of attempted coups and self-coups differ, so lists diverge on marginal cases.

concept: Characteristics of rebel and militant organizations
ids: CONF-046; CONF-047; CONF-048; CONF-008; CONF-052; CONF-049
how_to_choose: The Non-State Actor data code rebel strength, support and territorial control for UCDP dyads; FORGE records group origins and ideology; UCDP Actor gives identifiers; BAAD covers terrorist organizations; REVMOD and ROLE add organizational and leadership data. Merge through UCDP actor identifiers where available.

concept: Deliberate killing of civilians
ids: CONF-006; CONF-098; CONF-099; CONF-102; CONF-101; CONF-103
how_to_choose: UCDP One-sided Violence counts deaths from direct attacks on civilians since 1989; the PITF genocide/politicide list and Targeted Mass Killing data identify episodes with longer coverage; the Early Warning Project produces risk forecasts. Thresholds and intent criteria differ, producing different episode lists.

concept: Agreements to end or manage armed conflict
how_to_choose: The UCDP Peace Agreement data cover agreements between warring parties in UCDP conflicts; PA-X has a broader definition, more agreements and detailed provision coding; the Peace Accords Matrix measures implementation of comprehensive agreements; PSED codes power-sharing provisions. Choose PA-X for content analysis and UCDP for conflict-linked analyses.

concept: Third-party management of civil conflicts
ids: CONF-125; CONF-126; CONF-127; CONF-128; CONF-129; CONF-130
how_to_choose: The ETH/PRIO ceasefire data record ceasefires since 1989; Civil Wars Mediation and the UCDP MIC/MILC data code mediation and other third-party efforts with different time spans; the Peace Observatory and African Peace Processes data cover recent negotiations. Coverage periods rarely overlap fully, so long-run analyses must combine sources carefully.

concept: Politically relevant ethnic groups, access to power and mobilization
ids: CONF-137; CONF-145; CONF-146; CONF-135; GEO-002; CONF-138
how_to_choose: EPR codes power access of politically relevant ethnic groups from 1946 and links to UCDP conflicts (ACD2EPR) and to maps (GeoEPR); MAR (to 2006) selected groups at risk, which biases samples, and AMAR corrects this selection. The Self-Determination Movements data cover movements regardless of violence. Prefer EPR or AMAR to avoid selection on the dependent variable.

concept: Female participation in rebel organizations
how_to_choose: WAAR (Loken and Matfess) and WARD (Wood and Thomas) both code women's roles in rebel groups but differ in group samples, years and role categories; WAAR covers more groups and activities. Check which roles (combat, support, leadership) the question requires.

concept: Violence around elections
how_to_choose: ECAV codes events of electoral contention and violence (1990-2012); DECO records deadly electoral violence linked to UCDP events (1989-2017); CREV estimates country risk. Fatal-event data (DECO) and broader contention data (ECAV) answer different questions.

concept: Predictions of armed conflict and mass violence
how_to_choose: VIEWS produces monthly forecasts at country and grid level with published evaluation; Conflict Forecast uses news text; GCRI and the Early Warning Project produce annual risk scores. Compare forecasts on the same target (fatality threshold and horizon) before using them as covariates.

concept: Location and value of lootable and non-lootable resources
ids: CONF-147; CONF-148; CONF-150; CONF-151; CONF-152; PE-141
how_to_choose: PRIO's PETRODATA, DIADATA and DRUGDATA give point locations of resources up to the mid-2000s; the giant oil and gas fields data date discoveries; Ross-Mahdavi gives country-year oil and gas production. Use location data for subnational analyses and production or rents for country-level work.

concept: Killings, torture, disappearance and political imprisonment by states
how_to_choose: CIRIGHTS (successor to CIRI) and the Political Terror Scale code annual scores from State Department and Amnesty reports; the Fariss latent scores combine these with event-based sources and model changes in reporting standards; HRMI uses expert surveys; ITT codes allegations of torture. The 'changing standard of accountability' debate (Fariss 2014; Cingranelli and Filippov 2018) matters for trend analysis, so compare a standards-based score with the latent scores.

concept: Sexual violence and slavery by armed actors
how_to_choose: SVAC codes reported prevalence of sexual violence by state and non-state actors in active conflicts (1989-2023); CSAC codes slavery practices by armed groups. Both rely on reports whose coverage varies with international attention, so absence of reports is not evidence of absence.

concept: Public criticism of human rights violators
how_to_choose: Murdie-Davis code INGO shaming events, Ron-Ramos-Rodgers code Amnesty's reporting, and Lebovic-Voeten code UN Commission resolutions; the Human Rights Texts corpus provides the underlying report texts. Each measures a different shaming channel and period; most end before 2005.

concept: Ratification, reservations and national human rights institutions
how_to_choose: The OHCHR dashboard is the official source on treaty ratification; IHROC adds reservations and obligations; GANHRI accreditation and the Linos-Pegram data code national human rights institutions. Ratification dates from OHCHR should be preferred to compiled versions.

concept: Restrictions on association, expression and the internet
how_to_choose: The Digital Society Project gives expert-coded annual indicators of internet censorship and surveillance; CIVICUS Monitor rates civic space; Access Now records internet shutdowns; Freedom on the Net (REG-011) scores internet freedom. Transnational repression is covered by Freedom House and the AAAD. Event records (shutdowns, incidents) and expert scores measure different things.

concept: Demonstrations, riots and strikes
how_to_choose: SCAD (Africa and Latin America, to 2017) and Mass Mobilization (global, to 2020) are the standard cross-national protest datasets; MMAD focuses on autocracies; ACLED (CONF-032) records protests weekly. National projects (Crowd Counting Consortium, PolDem) give finer detail. All rely on news reports, so check coverage before comparing countries.

concept: Maximalist campaigns, resistance and revolutionary episodes
how_to_choose: NAVCO lists maximalist campaigns (1.x), codes campaign-years (2.x) and events (3.0); ARC adds organizational detail; Major Episodes of Contention, the Revolutionary Episodes data and RAQED use broader or different definitions of revolution. Results on campaign success depend on the population of campaigns included.

concept: Trials, truth commissions, amnesties, reparations and purges
how_to_choose: TJET (successor to the TJRC) is the broadest mechanism-level dataset; GTJD codes personnel purges and lustration; Varieties of Truth Commissions codes commission design; Post-Conflict Justice (CONF-134) covers post-conflict settings. Mechanisms are coded at different units (trial, commission, country-year), so aggregate carefully.

concept: Legal and violent crackdowns on civil society organizations
how_to_choose: Chaudhry's data combine administrative and violent crackdowns; Christensen-Weinstein and the Civil Society Restrictions dataset code laws on foreign funding and registration; the ICNL tracker covers COVID-19 measures. Coverage periods differ and most series end before 2015.

concept: Trafficking policies and estimates of forced labour
how_to_choose: The 3P index and U.S. TIP tier placements measure government policy effort; the Global Slavery Index estimates prevalence from surveys and models; CTDC and UNODC GLOTIP report identified victims. Prevalence estimates and counts of detected victims are not interchangeable.

concept: Killings by police
how_to_choose: Mapping Police Violence and the Washington Post database (2015-2024) are the main U.S. sources; Fatal Encounters ended in 2021; the Latin American lethal force monitor covers selected countries. Inclusion rules (shootings only vs all deaths) differ across sources.

concept: Killings and imprisonment of journalists and human rights defenders
how_to_choose: CPJ and the UNESCO observatory record killings of journalists with different confirmation rules; HRD-TK and Global Witness cover human rights and environmental defenders. Compare totals only after aligning definitions of motive and profession.

concept: Work stoppages and labour actions
how_to_choose: BLS records major U.S. work stoppages (1,000 workers or more), the Labor Action Tracker records all U.S. labour actions since 2021, and the Chilean observatory covers strikes in Chile; ILOSTAT (PE-105) provides cross-national strike statistics where reported. Thresholds differ widely.

concept: Full-text plenary debates with speaker metadata
ids: LEG-077; TEXT-009; TEXT-010; TEXT-011; TEXT-012; TEXT-014; TEXT-015; TEXT-016; TEXT-017; TEXT-018; TEXT-020; TEXT-021
how_to_choose: ParlSpeech gives harmonised speech-level corpora for nine parliaments ending 2016-2019; ParlaMint gives linguistically annotated corpora in a common TEI format for 29 European parliaments, mostly for 2015-2022; national corpora (LiPaD for Canada, the Katz-Alexander Australian debates, Norway, Finland, the Irish Dail database) offer longer histories for one country. Use ParlaMint for recent cross-national comparison and national corpora for long series; check speaker-party linkage and how procedural speech is handled.

concept: Floor speeches, hearings, press releases and newsletters
ids: TEXT-005; TEXT-006; TEXT-007; TEXT-024; TEXT-023; TEXT-054; TEXT-081; TEXT-078
how_to_choose: The Gentzkow-Shapiro-Taddy parsed Congressional Record (43rd-114th Congresses) is the standard floor-speech source and supersedes ICPSR 33501; ConSpeak is a newer speaker-aligned derivative with thinner documentation; ProQuest hearings XML is licensed. Press releases (TEXT-023, Grimmer's Senate releases TEXT-054), DCInbox e-newsletters and Tweets of Congress capture communication aimed at constituents rather than colleagues, so findings do not carry over between floor and outreach text.

concept: Speeches and statements in international settings
how_to_choose: The UN General Debate Corpus covers the annual speeches of all member states since 1946; the UNSC Debates corpus covers Security Council meetings and CR-UNSC its resolutions; FOCUSdata and the Chinese MFA press-conference corpus cover foreign-ministry communication. The General Debate corpus is the usual source for state preferences from text; report the version used, since most published work relies on the 2017 release.

concept: Presidential, ministerial and campaign speeches and debates
ids: TEXT-025; TEXT-026; TEXT-027; TEXT-028; TEXT-029; TEXT-030; TEXT-053
how_to_choose: The Miller Center files cover U.S. presidential speeches; the Annenberg/Pew archive and the 1960-1996 televised debate transcripts are legacy collections with limited access; the 2020 campaign-speech dataset covers one cycle; EUSpeech and the Rauh Commissioners corpus cover EU elites; DebatES covers Spanish election debates with annotations. Selection rules differ widely (which speeches count as major), so check inclusion criteria before comparing.

concept: Manifestos, press releases and party speeches
ids: PARTY-001; TEXT-031; TEXT-032; TEXT-033; TEXT-034; PARTY-054; PARTY-075; TEXT-058
how_to_choose: The Manifesto Project corpus provides coded manifestos for many countries; ManifestoVault and Polidoc provide full texts with different coverage; the Dutch-Danish congress speeches and South Korean campaign corpora are national; PARTYPRESS and the Gessler-Hunger data cover press releases; CampaignView covers U.S. House candidate platforms. Manifestos record formal programmes, while press releases track day-to-day issue emphasis.

concept: Word lists for sentiment, topics, emotion, morality and populism
ids: TEXT-039; TEXT-040; TEXT-041; TEXT-042; TEXT-043; TEXT-044; TEXT-045
how_to_choose: The Lexicoder Sentiment Dictionary is the standard English political-sentiment lexicon and Rauh's dictionary the German equivalent; the Lexicoder Topic and Discrete Emotions dictionaries cover topics and emotions; the Moral Foundations dictionaries (MFD, MFD 2.0 and the crowd-built eMFD) measure moral framing; the populism dictionaries are language- and period-specific. Validate any dictionary against hand-coded samples from the target corpus (van Atteveldt, van der Velden and Boukes 2021 found off-the-shelf dictionaries weak).

group: Labeled political text for supervised learning
concept: Human-annotated sentences and documents
ids: TEXT-046; TEXT-047; TEXT-048; TEXT-049; TEXT-050; TEXT-051; TEXT-052
how_to_choose: ClaimBuster (check-worthy claims), the Ideological Books Corpus, Convote (support or opposition in floor debates), PopBERT (populism in Bundestag speeches), ParlaSent (multilingual sentiment), HateBR (offensive comments) and FallacyES-Political (fallacies in debates) provide labels for training and validating classifiers. Annotation schemes, agreement levels and languages differ; report agreement statistics alongside model results.

concept: Press freedom, ownership, pluralism and journalism
ids: TEXT-063; TEXT-064; TEXT-065; REG-001; TEXT-066; TEXT-067; TEXT-068; TEXT-069; TEXT-070; TEXT-071
how_to_choose: RSF's World Press Freedom Index (2002 onward, method changes in 2013 and 2022) and Freedom House's Freedom of the Press (1980-2017 editions, discontinued) are expert assessments; the Global Media Freedom Dataset codes media freedom back to 1948; V-Dem also codes media freedom. Ownership and state control (Media Ownership Monitor, State Media Monitor), pluralism in Europe (Media Pluralism Monitor), media sustainability (VIBE, successor to MSI) and journalists' own views (Worlds of Journalism) measure different things. Do not splice series across method changes.

concept: Large collections of news articles and broadcasts
how_to_choose: Media Cloud indexes online news from tens of thousands of sources and serves URLs, metadata and counts (no redistributed full text); the Internet Archive TV News Archive and the Stanford Cable TV News Analyzer (frozen, data end October 2024) cover U.S. television; GDELT turns global news into event and tone records. Coverage depends on source lists that change over time, so fix the source set for longitudinal work.

concept: Platform data for research and archived actor corpora
ids: TEXT-072; TEXT-073; TEXT-074; TEXT-075; TEXT-076; TEXT-077; TEXT-078; TEXT-079; TEXT-080
how_to_choose: Open platform interfaces (CrowdTangle, closed 2024-08-14; Pushshift Reddit, now restricted) have given way to vetted access through the Meta Content Library and SOMAR at ICPSR. Archived corpora of political accounts (Twitter Parliamentarian Database, Trump Twitter Archive, Tweets of Congress) and Telegram collections remain usable for the periods they cover. Record platform terms and collection dates, and expect limits on redistribution.

concept: Television and online political ads
ids: TEXT-082; TEXT-083; TEXT-084; TEXT-085; TEXT-086; TEXT-087; TEXT-088; TEXT-089; TEXT-090
how_to_choose: The Wesleyan Media Project (licensed; 2024 data embargoed until after the 2026 elections) and its predecessor WiscAds code U.S. television ad airings and content; the Meta and Google ad libraries report online ads under platform-defined rules; CREATIVE harmonises Meta, Google and TV ads for the 2022 midterms; ProPublica's collections are past snapshots (the Facebook ads file is no longer downloadable); Nielsen Ad Intel and AdImpact are commercial. Platform libraries change definitions and omit most targeting detail, so compare across platforms with care.

concept: Fact-checks, claim labels and news-source ratings
ids: TEXT-091; TEXT-092; TEXT-093; TEXT-094; TEXT-095; TEXT-096
how_to_choose: ClaimReview feeds (Fact-Check Insights, Data Commons) aggregate published fact-checks; LIAR and FakeNewsNet are labeled benchmarks built from fact-checking sites; the Lin et al. aggregate ratings (open) and NewsGuard (commercial) rate news domains. Domain ratings and claim labels measure different things, and every benchmark inherits the fact-checkers' choice of which claims to check.

concept: Country-level ethnic, linguistic and religious diversity
ids: IDENT-001; IDENT-002; IDENT-003; IDENT-004; IDENT-005; IDENT-006; IDENT-007; IDENT-008; CONF-137
how_to_choose: Fearon (about 1990s, 160 countries) and Alesina et al. (about 2000, up to 215 countries) are static cross-sections and the most cited; Roeder gives 1961 and 1985 values; HIEF and CREG give annual series for 1945-2013; Posner's PREG counts only politically relevant groups, and EPR codes groups by access to power. Use HIEF or CREG for change over time, PREG or EPR when political relevance matters, and Desmet-Ortuno-Wacziarg when the depth of linguistic cleavages matters. Selway's measures add cross-cutting structure that single indices ignore.

concept: Maps and spatial estimates of where ethnic groups live
ids: IDENT-011; IDENT-012; IDENT-013; IDENT-014; IDENT-015; GEO-002; IDENT-010
how_to_choose: GREG digitizes the maps of the Soviet Atlas Narodov Mira (global); GeoEPR maps politically relevant groups over time; SIDE interpolates DHS survey data into fine-grained maps for 47 low- and middle-income countries; the Murdock map and Ethnographic Atlas describe pre-colonial African and world societies; LEDA links ethnic categories across these sources. Choose by period and purpose: historical homelands (Murdock, Ethnographic Atlas), mid-century settlement (GREG), politically relevant groups (GeoEPR), recent fine-grained distributions (SIDE, Gershman-Rivera).

concept: Minorities in legislatures, cabinets and organizations
ids: IDENT-017; IDENT-018; IDENT-019; IDENT-020; IDENT-021; IDENT-023; IDENT-024; IDENT-033; CONF-137; IDENT-132
how_to_choose: EPR codes executive power access by group; Francois-Rainer-Trebbi code the ethnicity of African cabinet ministers; Ruedin (2006 snapshot), POREM-CEE and the Muslim-origin MPs data cover legislatures; Pathways to Power covers MPs of immigrant origin; SPINPER covers Indian legislators' caste and religion (restricted); Huber measures ethnic voting from surveys. Coverage windows are short and coding of group membership differs, so check definitions before combining. EGMR (2026) adds which ethnic groups armies recruit from or exclude, a military counterpart to cabinet- and legislature-based measures.

concept: Rights and accommodation of minorities and Indigenous peoples
ids: IDENT-025; IDENT-028; IDENT-029; IDENT-030; IDENT-031; IDENT-027; IDENT-039; IDENT-040; IDENT-136
how_to_choose: The Multiculturalism Policy Index scores policies for immigrant, national and Indigenous minorities in Western democracies (benchmark years 1980-2020); INDILEX covers Indigenous legislation in Latin America; LAWD covers language laws; Peoples under Threat ranks risk of mass violence; Lieberman-Singh code ethnic categories in censuses; RASM and RMAR cover religious minorities. Most are static or irregular, so use them for cross-sectional comparison. The Nation-Building Policies preview (2026) codes assimilationist and exclusionary state policies, but only its USSR module and a cultural-elimination file are public so far.

concept: Shares of religious groups by country
ids: IDENT-043; IDENT-044; IDENT-046; IDENT-047; IDENT-048; IDENT-050; IDENT-051; IDENT-005; IDENT-002
how_to_choose: The COW World Religion Data (1945-2010, five-year intervals) and RCS-Dem (annual, from 1900 or 1800 to 2015) are open; the World Religion and World Christian databases (licensed) give long series and projections; Pew's 2010 and 2020 estimates are the best-documented recent benchmarks (the 2025 release revises earlier Pew 2010 figures); Barro-McCleary and Flora cover historical benchmarks. Expect differences in how 'religiously unaffiliated' and folk religions are counted.

concept: Government regulation, support and restriction of religion
ids: IDENT-038; IDENT-039; IDENT-041; IDENT-054; IDENT-055; IDENT-056; IDENT-057; IDENT-058
how_to_choose: RAS (1990-2014 public; RAS4 to 2023 not yet posted) codes official religion, support, regulation and discrimination in detail; Pew's Government Restrictions and Social Hostilities indices (2007-2022) are annual and widely used; the Grim-Finke indices are their frozen predecessor; GRP codes state religious preference since 1800; the Islamic Constitutions Index is a single snapshot. Open Doors' World Watch List is an advocacy ranking of Christian persecution and should not be used as a general measure.

concept: Religious dimensions of armed conflict and communal violence
ids: IDENT-059; IDENT-060; IDENT-061; CONF-058; IDENT-053; CONF-137; IDENT-131
how_to_choose: RELAC codes the religious identity and claims of conflict parties (1975-2015); PRIO Religious Cleavages codes religious differences between conflict parties (1946-2004); Varshney-Wilkinson record Hindu-Muslim riots in India (1950-1995); A-Religion adds religion to AMAR groups. Choose RELAC for whether religion is part of the incompatibility and PRIO for religious difference alone. ICOW identity claims (1946-2021) cover interstate claims over the treatment of shared ethnic groups (kin across borders), a different unit from the intrastate conflict data here.

concept: How many migrants live where, and how many move each year
ids: IDENT-068; IDENT-069; IDENT-070; IDENT-071; IDENT-072; IDENT-073; IDENT-074; IDENT-075; IDENT-076; IDENT-078; IDENT-134
how_to_choose: UN DESA's International Migrant Stock (1990-2024) is the standard global stock series; the World Bank database gives bilateral stocks for 1960-2000; Abel-Cohen estimate bilateral flows from stock differences (1990-2020); DEMIG TOTAL and C2C compile recorded flows (to 2011, frozen); OECD IMD and Eurostat give official flows for their members. Stocks mix foreign-born and foreign-citizen definitions, and estimated flows depend on the method, so state which flow measure is used. Gaskin and Abel (2026) give model-based annual bilateral flow estimates for 1990-2023; treat them as estimates with uncertainty, not counts, and compare against the Abel-Cohen five-year series before relying on single dyads.

concept: Refugees, asylum-seekers and internally displaced people
ids: IDENT-079; IDENT-080; IDENT-081; IDENT-082; IDENT-083; IDENT-118; CONF-141
how_to_choose: UNHCR's Refugee Data Finder (1951 onward) is the reference for refugees and asylum-seekers; IDMC's GIDD covers internal displacement (conflict and disasters); the CSP series (1964-2008) is frozen; Zhou-Shaver geolocate UNHCR sites; EPR-ER links refugees to ethnic groups; the Missing Migrants Project records deaths in transit. Figures depend on registration and recognition practices, so cross-country comparison needs care.

concept: Rules for entry, stay, asylum and integration
ids: IDENT-084; IDENT-085; IDENT-086; IDENT-087; IDENT-088; IDENT-091; IDENT-092; IDENT-093; IDENT-094; IDENT-095; IDENT-135
how_to_choose: IMPIC (33 OECD countries, 1980-2018) measures policy levels; DEMIG POLICY records about 6,500 policy changes in 45 countries to 2014 (changes, not levels); HIP and Peters's dataset cover low-skill immigration policy back to 1783; DWRAP covers refugee and asylum law worldwide (1951-2022); MIPEX and CIVIX measure integration requirements; POLMIG extends DEMIG-style change data for Europe to 2019. Use IMPIC or MIPEX for levels, DEMIG or POLMIG for the timing of reforms, HIP for long-run history and DWRAP for refugee policy outside the OECD. The Refugee Dispersal Policy data (2025) are narrower: how European states allocate asylum seekers across their territory.

concept: Citizenship law, dual citizenship and diaspora policy
ids: IDENT-098; IDENT-099; IDENT-100; IDENT-101; IDENT-102; IDENT-103; ELEC-018; ELEC-033; IDENT-133
how_to_choose: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset (191 states, 2020-2024; dual citizenship back to 1960) is the most complete de jure source; MACIMIDE covers dual citizenship for emigrants (1960-2020); CITRIX scores inclusiveness of citizenship regimes (1980-2019); CITLAW is an older European indicator set; EMIX and EMIX-Asia score emigrant policies; emigrant voting rights are in ELEC-018 and ELEC-033. All code law on the books; implementation can differ. For dyad-level questions (which pairs of countries mutually accept dual citizenship), use the GLOBALCIT dyadic dataset rather than deriving pairs from country-level indicators.

concept: Visas, passports, border walls and crossings
ids: IDENT-085; IDENT-105; IDENT-106; IDENT-107; IDENT-108; IDENT-109; IDENT-110; IDENT-128; IDENT-129; IDENT-130
how_to_choose: DEMIG VISA (1973-2013) and the Visa Network Data (1969, 2010) code visa requirements; the Global Visa Cost Dataset adds fees (2019); the Henley Passport Index is a commercial ranking; border walls are covered by Hassner-Wittenberg, Carter-Poast (1800-2014) and the new geolocated Kenwick-Pauselli-Simmons data; Border Crossings of the World (1993-2025) and the Border Permeability Dataset measure border infrastructure and openness. Prefer the Kenwick-Simmons data for recent, verifiable locations.

concept: Surveys of migrants, origin communities and children of immigrants
ids: IDENT-111; IDENT-112; IDENT-113; IDENT-114; IDENT-115; IDENT-116; IDENT-117; OPIN-126
how_to_choose: MMP (Mexico and Central America) and LAMP use ethnosurveys in origin and destination communities; MAFE covers African-European migration; the New Immigrant Survey follows U.S. green-card recipients; CILS and CILS4EU follow children of immigrants in the U.S. and four European countries; LINES (OPIN-126) covers Latino immigrants' politics. Access is mostly by registration, and recent LAMP files were not downloadable at the time of checking.

concept: Share of seats held by women
ids: GENDER-001; GENDER-005; GENDER-002; GENDER-012; LEG-041; LEG-033; REG-001
how_to_choose: IPU (GENDER-001) is the current reference series; Paxton-Green-Hughes (GENDER-005) revises early IPU values and is better for 1945-2003; EIGE WMID (GENDER-012) adds Europe's regional and executive bodies; V-Dem and the Global Legislators Database offer gender as one variable among many.

group: Women in executives, parties and international organizations
concept: Women in cabinets, party leadership and IO leadership
ids: EXEC-004; EXEC-019; GENDER-002; GENDER-008; GENDER-009; GENDER-010; IR-116
how_to_choose: WhoGov (EXEC-004) is the broadest cabinet panel; the IPU-UN Women map (GENDER-002) gives snapshots; O'Brien (GENDER-008) covers party leaders in 11 democracies to 2013; GWL Voices (GENDER-009) counts IO heads and senior staff; GenDip (IR-116) covers ambassadors.

concept: Women in local councils and regions
ids: GENDER-006; GENDER-007; GENDER-012; GENDER-014; ELEC-075; ELEC-110
how_to_choose: UN Women's SDG 5.5.1b data (GENDER-006) are the only global series but start in 2020; Sundstrom's European regional file (GENDER-007) is a snapshot to 2013; for U.S. and Canadian local office use the election databases in ELEC.

concept: Adoption and design of quotas
how_to_choose: QAROT (GENDER-004) is the panel to 2015 with thresholds, sanctions and placement rules; IDEA's database (GENDER-003) has current rules, including party and subnational quotas, but no bulk download or history.

concept: Laws and institutions affecting women's status
ids: GENDER-027; GENDER-025; GENDER-026; GENDER-024; GENDER-039; HR-001; CONST-003
how_to_choose: WBL (GENDER-027) codes codified economic law annually; SIGI and GID-DB (GENDER-025/026) add social institutions and practice in five editions; WomanStats (GENDER-024) contrasts law and practice; CIRIGHTS (HR-001) gives women's rights scores within a human-rights panel; CONST-003 covers constitutional provisions.

concept: Overall gender equality or women's status
ids: GENDER-028; GENDER-029; GENDER-030; GENDER-031; GENDER-023; PE-032
how_to_choose: The Global Gender Gap Index (GENDER-028) measures outcome gaps truncated at parity; EIGE's index (GENDER-029) is the most detailed for the EU; the SDG Gender Index and the WPS Index cover broader agendas; UNDP's GII (PE-032) is common in development studies. Check weighting and edition changes before pooling years.

concept: Official sex-disaggregated indicators
ids: GENDER-032; GENDER-033; GENDER-034; GENDER-035; GENDER-036; GENDER-037; GENDER-038; PE-001
how_to_choose: The World Bank portal (GENDER-032) has the longest series and an API; UN Women and UNSD (GENDER-033/034) follow the SDG and minimum-set frameworks; EIGE, UNECE and ECLAC give regional depth. Cite the original producer of each indicator.

concept: Feminist mobilization and women's organizations
how_to_choose: RNGS (GENDER-018) codes policy debates in 13 Western democracies to 2001; WINGO (GENDER-019) counts women's INGO memberships to 2013; the Feminist Mobilization Index (GENDER-020) gives decadal scores to 2015; FEMPOWER (GENDER-021) maps women's organizations to 2023; Women in Resistance (HR-071) covers women in protest campaigns.

concept: Public support for gender equality
how_to_choose: Public Gender Egalitarianism (GENDER-022) pools many surveys into country-year latent estimates with uncertainty; the Gender Social Norms Index (GENDER-023) uses two WVS waves; PUSH*BACK*LASH (OPIN-041) harmonizes European individual-level data.

concept: Abortion law and access
how_to_choose: WHO's GAPD (GENDER-044) is the reference global record of current abortion law; Canning's database (GENDER-045) gave historical series but is discontinued; for the United States use Guttmacher's public-use data (GENDER-046) and the Myers facility database (GENDER-047) for access. The CRR map (GENDER-048) is an advocacy classification without structured data.

concept: Leave, care and gender equality policy
ids: GENDER-049; GENDER-050; GENDER-051; GENDER-055; POLICY-048; POLICY-039; POLICY-040
how_to_choose: EPLP (GENDER-050) is the long European panel; GDParL (GENDER-049) is global but has three snapshots; the OECD Family Database (POLICY-048) and PROSPERED (POLICY-039) give OECD series; GEPOD (GENDER-055) codes broader gender equality policy in Europe.

concept: CEDAW commitments and human-rights recommendations
how_to_choose: CEDAW ROCS (GENDER-039) codes ratification, reservations and objections; HR-097 compares reservations across 23 treaties; WR2D2 and WRCD (GENDER-040/041) code Council of Europe recommendations and compliance for 2007-2016.

concept: Gender-based violence and political violence targeting women
how_to_choose: ACLED's PVTW (GENDER-043) records events of political violence targeting women; UN Women's database (GENDER-042) lists government measures, not incidence; UNODC (HR-035) has femicide statistics; SVAC (HR-012) covers conflict-related sexual violence; WomanStats scales add law-versus-practice judgments.

concept: Legal recognition and rights of LGBTQ+ people
ids: POLICY-073; POLICY-074; POLICY-072; GENDER-068; GENDER-061; GENDER-064; GENDER-066; GENDER-069; GENDER-067; GENDER-070
how_to_choose: ILGA (POLICY-073) is the global legal reference; GILRHO (GENDER-068) gives a scholarly year-by-year index to 2011; TRIP (GENDER-061) covers transgender rights to 2021; Rainbow Map (POLICY-074) and TGEU (GENDER-064) are European advocacy indices; MAP and HRC (GENDER-067/070) cover U.S. states.

concept: Public acceptance and LGBTQ+ officeholders
ids: GENDER-065; OPIN-040; GENDER-062; GENDER-063; GENDER-073; GENDER-074
how_to_choose: The Global Acceptance Index (GENDER-065) and Support for Gay Rights (OPIN-040) both pool surveys; for officeholders, Queer Politics at Princeton (GENDER-062) is offline and Victory Institute (GENDER-063) covers the United States; USTS and TransPop (GENDER-073/074) are the main U.S. transgender surveys.

concept: Treaties, membership and negotiation participation
ids: ENV-001; ENV-002; ENV-003; ENV-004; ENV-006; ENV-007; INFRA-031
how_to_choose: IEADB (ENV-001) is the reference list of agreements and memberships; TREND (ENV-002) codes environmental clauses in trade agreements; TFDD (ENV-003) covers river treaties; UNFCCC attendance and YouthEarth (ENV-006/007) cover who takes part in negotiations; manytreaties (INFRA-031) links treaty datasets.

concept: NDCs, net-zero targets and their assessment
how_to_choose: Climate Watch (ENV-009) is the most current NDC content source; NDC Explorer (ENV-010) is frozen at 2021; Net Zero Tracker (ENV-013) covers national, subnational and corporate targets; Climate Action Tracker (ENV-012) rates ambition with its own method; the Transparency Adherence Index (ENV-008) measures reporting quality.

concept: Cities, firms and transnational initiatives
how_to_choose: CoAct (ENV-015) codes cooperative initiatives over time; CDP's open data (ENV-016) give city and region disclosures; the UNFCCC portal (ENV-014) lists commitments but offers no download.

concept: Laws, policies and court cases
how_to_choose: CCLW (ENV-017) is the global law inventory; the Sabin database (ENV-018) is the reference for litigation; the Oxford Climate Policy Monitor (ENV-019) adds detailed coding for 30-plus countries; the Sabin Backtracker and Harvard EELP trackers (ENV-020/022) follow U.S. federal rollbacks.

concept: Adopted climate policies and their stringency
ids: ENV-023; ENV-024; ENV-025; ENV-026; ENV-027; ENV-028; POLICY-028; ENV-118
how_to_choose: CAPMF (ENV-024) gives comparable stringency scores for 50 countries; EPS (ENV-025) is its frozen predecessor; the Climate Policy Database (ENV-023) and GCCMPD (ENV-027) list individual policies; IEA Policies (ENV-026) is broad but undocumented; CONSENSUS (POLICY-028) codes policy portfolios. The OECD IFCMA Climate Policy Database (ENV-118, first edition 2025) counts policy instruments with its own typology and complements CAPMF's stringency scores.

concept: Carbon taxes, ETS coverage and prices
how_to_choose: The World Carbon Pricing Database (ENV-029) is the research panel; the World Bank dashboard (ENV-030) and ICAP (ENV-031) are current descriptive trackers; OECD Effective Carbon Rates (ENV-033) combine taxes and permits; EU ETS registry data (ENV-034) and EUETS.INFO (ENV-035) give installation-level compliance; Berkeley's database (ENV-036) covers voluntary offsets.

group: Fossil-fuel subsidies and public energy finance
concept: Government support for fossil fuels
how_to_choose: The OECD-IISD Fossil Fuel Subsidy Tracker (ENV-032) is the maintained global series; the Energy Policy Tracker (ENV-042) covered pandemic-era G20 commitments only.

concept: Public and private climate finance flows
how_to_choose: OECD Rio-marker data (ENV-037; underlying records in IR-133) are the main donor-reported series and have been criticised for over-reporting; Climate Funds Update (ENV-038) tracks multilateral climate funds; CPI's Global Landscape (ENV-039) adds private finance; the Reuters-Stanford data (ENV-040) recode UNFCCC reports; PLAID (ENV-041) codes aid projects' environmental impact.

concept: Greenhouse gas emissions by country
how_to_choose: The Global Carbon Budget (ENV-045) and PRIMAP-hist (ENV-044) give long series; EDGAR (ENV-043) covers all gases since 1970 with its own model; Climate Watch (ENV-047) repackages several sources; UNFCCC submissions (ENV-048) are what governments report; CDIAC (ENV-046) is the legacy series; CEADs (ENV-051) is the main source for Chinese provinces.

concept: Emissions attributed to plants, firms and producers
how_to_choose: EPA GHGRP (ENV-105) is reported U.S. facility data; Climate TRACE (ENV-049) estimates assets worldwide from remote sensing and models; Carbon Majors (ENV-050) attributes emissions to fossil-fuel producers; Global Energy Monitor (ENV-058) and the WRI power-plant database (ENV-059, frozen) give plant-level infrastructure.

concept: Energy production, consumption and electricity
how_to_choose: IEA balances (ENV-053) are the most detailed but commercial; the Energy Institute review (ENV-054) and UNSD (ENV-055) are free alternatives with long series; EIA (ENV-052) has an open API with international data; Ember (ENV-056) is the most current for electricity; OPEC (ENV-057) covers oil producers.

concept: Overall environmental performance
how_to_choose: EPI (ENV-066) is the standard index but its editions cannot be pooled; ESI (ENV-067) is its predecessor; QoG-EI (ENV-068) merges environmental variables in one country-year file; the Environmental Democracy Index (ENV-069) codes procedural rights in 2014 only; CCPI (ENV-070) is an advocacy ranking; the SDG Index (PE-054) adds sustainability goals.

concept: Exposure and vulnerability to climate hazards
how_to_choose: ND-GAIN (ENV-073) has the longest annual series; INFORM (ENV-074) targets humanitarian risk; WorldRiskIndex (ENV-075) has method breaks in 2022 and 2026; the Climate Risk Index (ENV-076) counts past losses and changed source; Aqueduct (ENV-077) covers water risk; SPEI (ENV-079) is a physical drought index that must be aggregated to political units.

concept: Public attitudes towards climate change
