how_to_choose: In the United States, YCOM (ENV-080) gives modelled small-area estimates, CCAM (ENV-081) and NSEE (ENV-082) provide microdata, and Bergquist-Warshaw (ENV-083) give state series; cross-nationally, use the Meta-Yale survey (ENV-084), the World Risk Poll (ENV-085), the ISSP environment modules (OPIN-006) or the GCCS (ENV-087); UNDP's Peoples' Climate Vote (ENV-086) is less documented. For subnational estimates outside the United States, the Bergquist et al. global national and sub-national concern estimates (ENV-117, 2010-2022) extend the state-level approach worldwide.

concept: Environmental positions and mobilization
ids: ENV-088; ENV-089; ENV-090; ENV-091; PARTY-001; PARTY-003; HR-093; HR-082
how_to_choose: Policlim (ENV-088) codes climate content in manifestos; Carter et al. (ENV-089) cover six countries to 2015; MARPOR (PARTY-001) and CHES (PARTY-003) give general environmental positions; the LCV scorecard (ENV-090) rates U.S. legislators by an advocacy group's vote selection; the Carnegie tracker (ENV-091), Protest for a Future (HR-093) and PolDem (HR-082) cover protest.

concept: Environmental conflicts, water disputes and justice
how_to_choose: EJAtlas (ENV-092) documents conflicts but is a convenience sample; the Water Conflict Chronology (ENV-093) and WARICC (ENV-094) cover water disputes; Global Witness (HR-040) counts killings of environmental defenders; resource-conflict data sit in CONF (CONF-151, CONF-063).

concept: Natural disaster events and losses
how_to_choose: EM-DAT (ENV-095) is the global event list; GDIS (ENV-096) geocodes it; DesInventar (ENV-097) has national loss databases of uneven quality; for the United States, NOAA's billion-dollar series (ENV-098) ended in 2024 and continues at Climate Central (ENV-099), while Storm Events (ENV-100), FEMA declarations (ENV-101) and the National Risk Index (ENV-102) cover events, federal responses and risk.

group: U.S. environmental regulation and environmental justice
concept: Pollution, enforcement and environmental-justice screening
how_to_choose: ECHO (ENV-103) gives facility inspections and enforcement; TRI (ENV-104) reports toxic releases; CAMPD (ENV-106) covers power-plant emissions and allowance trading; EJScreen and CEJST (ENV-108/109) were withdrawn in 2025 and survive as archived copies; the CDC's EJI (ENV-110) is a health-oriented alternative.

concept: Deforestation, land acquisitions and protection
how_to_choose: Global Forest Change (ENV-060) is the global pixel-level forest-loss series (with a 2011 method break); MapBiomas (ENV-061) gives annual land-cover maps for Brazil and other countries; Land Matrix (ENV-062) records large-scale land deals; WDPA (ENV-063) maps protected areas.

concept: Firm environmental, social and governance ratings
how_to_choose: All are commercial and their ratings diverge across vendors (Berg, Koelbel and Rigobon 2022); KLD (ENV-113) is the long legacy series to 2019; CDP (ENV-115) holds firms' own disclosures; Trucost (ENV-116) estimates emissions for non-reporting firms.

concept: Subnational administrative units worldwide
how_to_choose: GADM (GEO-003) is the deepest but closed-licensed snapshot; geoBoundaries (GEO-004) is open and year-tagged; FAO GAUL (GEO-005) and UN SALB (GEO-006) are official UN products with uneven updates; OCHA COD-AB (GEO-007) is the humanitarian standard; World Bank boundaries (GEO-008) follow the Bank's official positions on disputed areas.

concept: State borders and maritime zones
how_to_choose: LSIB (GEO-009) gives current U.S.-recognised land borders; Marine Regions (GEO-010) gives maritime zones; CShapes (GEO-011) gives historical state borders from 1886.

concept: Borders and political entities over time
how_to_choose: CShapes (GEO-011) is the standard for modern states; Cliopatria (GEO-012) covers polities from 3400 BCE; HistoGIS (GEO-013), MPIDR (GEO-014), CHGIS (GEO-016), GBHGIS (GEO-017) and the Atlas of Historical County Boundaries (GEO-057) give historical subnational units; Euratlas (GEO-015) is commercial.

concept: Grid-cell units and population surfaces
how_to_choose: PRIO-GRID (GEO-018) is the political-science grid; GHSL (GEO-021) and WorldPop (GEO-020) are maintained population grids; GPWv4 (GEO-019) is frozen; LandScan (GEO-022) models ambient population; HRSL (GEO-023) is high-resolution but single-year; HYDE (GEO-024) gives long-run historical estimates.

concept: Remote-sensed and geographic covariates
how_to_choose: Use the harmonized DMSP-VIIRS series (GEO-025) for long panels; EOG products (GEO-026) and Black Marble (GEO-027) are the raw sources with a sensor break in 2012-2013; travel time (GEO-028), ruggedness (GEO-029) and roads (GEO-030) are mostly time-invariant; GeoQuery (GEO-031) extracts many layers to administrative units.

concept: Gridded and regional GDP and development
how_to_choose: DOSE (GEO-034) compiles official regional accounts; gridded GDP (GEO-033) models output to grid cells from 1990; G-Econ (GEO-032) is frozen at 2005; Roses-Wolf (GEO-035) gives European regions from 1900; GLocal (GEO-036) and the subnational HDI (PE-049) cover development.

concept: Elections below the national level and district maps
ids: ELEC-138; ELEC-139; ELEC-141; ELEC-142; ELEC-143; GEO-038; GEO-039; GEO-040; GEO-047; GEO-084; GEO-085
how_to_choose: Schakel's regional election data (ELEC-138) cover European regions; country collections (Poland ELEC-139, Canada ELEC-141, Brazil ELEC-142, Chile ELEC-143) give local results; official boundary files come from Canada, Australia and the UK (GEO-039/040/047); SUNGEO (GEO-038) links results to boundaries but was offline on 2026-11-06. For Canada before 2003, use the historical federal district boundaries of Taylor, Lucas, Kirby and Hewitt (GEO-084, 1867-2021); UK census boundaries and postcode directories come from UK Data Service Census Support (GEO-085).

concept: Regional institutions and subnational regimes
how_to_choose: ISED (GEO-044) scores subnational electoral democracy; QoG EU Regional (GEO-042, frozen) and OECD regional statistics (GEO-043) give regional covariates; LocGov (GEO-001) surveys local elites; Norway and Sweden have long local-government panels (GEO-045/046). The Regional Authority Index sits under CONST.

concept: Village, municipal and district data for large countries
ids: GEO-048; GEO-049; GEO-050; GEO-051; AREA-006; AREA-007; AREA-008
how_to_choose: SHRUG (GEO-048) links Indian village and town data across censuses; DataMeet (GEO-049) supplies community-built Indian boundaries; IBGE (GEO-050) and INEGI (GEO-051) are the official Brazilian and Mexican geographies; commercial Chinese and Indian statistics platforms are AREA-006 to AREA-008.

concept: Census boundaries and small-area tables
how_to_choose: TIGER/Line (GEO-052) is the official current geography; NHGIS (GEO-053) gives historical boundaries and tables from 1790; ACS (GEO-054) and data.census.gov (GEO-055) supply current tables; PEP (GEO-056) gives annual estimates; the Newberry atlas (GEO-057) maps historical county boundaries.

concept: Linking geographies and redistricting data
ids: GEO-058; GEO-059; GEO-060; GEO-061; GEO-062; GEO-063; ELEC-144; ELEC-116
how_to_choose: Census relationship files (GEO-058) and Geocorr (GEO-059) link current geographies; the Ferrara-Testa-Zhou crosswalks (GEO-060) harmonise counties and districts from 1790; LTDB (GEO-061) normalises tracts to 2010 boundaries; Dave's Redistricting (GEO-062) and precinct reallocations (GEO-063) support redistricting analysis; congressional district shapefiles are ELEC-116.

concept: District-level election and demographic data
how_to_choose: The Wolf spatiotemporal database (ELEC-145) joins returns to district boundaries for 1896-2014; Adler (ELEC-146) and Lublin (ELEC-147) give district demographics for earlier periods; Lewis et al. shapefiles (ELEC-116) supply the boundaries.

group: U.S. local government structure and finance
concept: Local governments, finances and forms
how_to_choose: The Census finance surveys (GEO-064) are the official source; the Government Finance Database (GEO-065) harmonises them for 1967-2012; FiSC (GEO-066) makes city finances comparable by adding overlapping governments; ICMA (GEO-067) covers form of government; incorporation dates (GEO-069) and school districts (GEO-070) complete the structure.

concept: Local meetings, officials and news
ids: GEO-071; GEO-072; GEO-073; GEO-074; ELEC-110; ELEC-111
how_to_choose: LocalView (GEO-071) collects public-meeting videos and transcripts; Council Data Project (GEO-072) covers a few cities; CivicPulse (GEO-073) surveys local officials; Medill (GEO-074) maps news deserts; local election results are in ELEC-110 and ELEC-111.

concept: State partisan control, policy and money
ids: AREA-001; AREA-002; AREA-003; AREA-004; OPIN-145; POLICY-008
how_to_choose: Klarner's partisan balance (AREA-001) is the long series to 2011; NCSL tables (AREA-002) give current composition; CHORUS (AREA-003) codes state policy choice; FollowTheMoney (AREA-004) is frozen while merged into OpenSecrets; Berry et al. ideology measures are OPIN-145; Correlates of State Policy is under POLICY.

concept: Neighbourhood social and economic indicators
how_to_choose: The Social Capital Atlas (GEO-075) and Opportunity Atlas (GEO-076) give tract- and county-level measures from administrative and Facebook data; the Census Planning Database (GEO-077) summarises ACS indicators; LTDB (GEO-061) supports change over time.

concept: Subscription mapping and demographic tools
how_to_choose: Social Explorer (GEO-078) is the most listed and adds historical census tables; PolicyMap (GEO-079) and SimplyAnalytics (GEO-080) are mapping tools; NCDB (GEO-081) normalises tracts but LTDB or NHGIS are open alternatives (Logan, Stults and Xu 2016); cite the underlying public sources in replication files.

concept: National long-run statistical series
ids: HIST-001; HIST-002; HIST-007; HIST-008; HIST-010; HIST-011; HIST-014; HIST-019; HIST-020; HIST-021; PE-021
how_to_choose: HSUS (HIST-001) and Historical Statistics of Canada (HIST-002) cover North America; histat (HIST-007), Swiss, Swedish, Norwegian and Italian collections cover Europe; MOxLAD (HIST-019) covers Latin America; LTES and the Historical Statistics of Japan (HIST-020/021) cover Japan; Mitchell (PE-021) is the cross-national reference.

concept: Long-run GDP and macroeconomic series
ids: HIST-010; HIST-012; HIST-018; HIST-022; HIST-038; HIST-039; HIST-040; HIST-041; PE-004
how_to_choose: Maddison (PE-004) is the cross-national standard; Swedish (HIST-010), Dutch (HIST-018), Prussian (HIST-012), Asian (HIST-022) and UK millennium data (HIST-041) give national depth; Barro-Ursua (HIST-039) and the Long-Term Productivity Database (HIST-040) give long panels; the NBER Macrohistory files (HIST-038) are frozen.

concept: Individual-level historical census records
ids: HIST-025; HIST-026; HIST-027; HIST-028; HIST-029; HIST-030; HIST-031; HIST-032
how_to_choose: IPUMS full count (HIST-025) is the U.S. standard; MLP (HIST-026) and the Census Linking Project (HIST-029) link people across censuses; NAPP (HIST-027, superseded) harmonised North Atlantic samples; I-CeM (HIST-028) covers Britain; Canadian, Dutch and Norwegian sources (HIST-030 to 032) are partly restricted.

group: Historical U.S. county and local data
concept: Historical county, city and state data
ids: HIST-003; HIST-004; HIST-005; HIST-006; GEO-053; GEO-057
how_to_choose: The Haines collection (HIST-003) gives county data from 1790; the County and City Data Books (HIST-004) are discontinued; Census working papers (HIST-005) give historical population tables; Sylla-Legler-Wallis (HIST-006) covers state and local finance before 1915; NHGIS (GEO-053) supplies boundaries.

concept: Long-run prices, wages, interest and exchange rates
ids: HIST-033; HIST-034; HIST-035; HIST-036; HIST-037; HIST-042; HIST-043
how_to_choose: MeasuringWorth (HIST-034) gives ready long series; GPIH (HIST-037) and MEMDB (HIST-035) cover pre-modern prices and wages; the IISH list (HIST-036) is discontinued; Swedish monetary statistics (HIST-043) and Historical Financial Statistics (HIST-042) cover money and finance; EH.Net (HIST-033) hosts many smaller datasets.

concept: Public revenues and debt before 1945
how_to_choose: The European State Finance Database (HIST-044) covers c. 1200-1815; Sylla-Legler-Wallis (HIST-006) covers U.S. state and local finance; colonial French public finances (HIST-050) cover 1830-1962; several article panels on fiscal capacity have no public release.

concept: Historical polities, institutions and complexity
ids: HIST-051; HIST-052; HIST-053; HIST-054; HIST-055; GEO-012; GEO-011
how_to_choose: Seshat (HIST-051) codes institutions for hundreds of past polities; MOROS (HIST-052) codes state survival; ICOW state names (HIST-053) and Abramson's European states (HIST-055) give state lists; Taagepera's polity sizes (HIST-054) are thinly documented; Cliopatria and CShapes (GEO) give borders.

concept: Colonial rule and its institutions
ids: HIST-045; HIST-046; HIST-047; HIST-048; HIST-049; HIST-050
how_to_choose: COLDAT (HIST-045) gives colonial dates; ICOW (HIST-046) gives colonial rulers and independence; the Colonial Transformation Dataset (HIST-047) codes colonial impacts; Imperial Roots of Global Trade (HIST-048) covers empires' trade; HGIS de las Indias (HIST-049) and French colonial finances (HIST-050) cover specific empires.

concept: The slave trade and historical migration
how_to_choose: SlaveVoyages (HIST-058/059) is the reference for voyages; Manning and Liu's routes (HIST-060) and Nunn's export estimates (HIST-061) give country-level series; the World Migration Matrix (HIST-062) traces population ancestry from 1500.

concept: Wars and violence before the modern data era
ids: HIST-063; HIST-064; HIST-065; HIST-066; HIST-067; HIST-068; HIST-069
how_to_choose: Brecke (HIST-063) spans 1400 onward but is unfinished; Fettweis (HIST-064) and War Dummies (HIST-065) cover early modern Europe; Warring-States Japan (HIST-066) covers 1467-1600; the Old Terrorism dataset (HIST-067), interwar arms trade (HIST-068) and HiSCoD (HIST-069) cover specific forms; COW data begin in 1816.

concept: Elite individuals in aggregate
ids: HIST-070; HIST-071; HIST-072; HIST-073; EXEC-054; LEG-088; LEG-089; LEG-090; LEG-091; LEG-092
how_to_choose: CBDB (HIST-070) covers Chinese officials; the cross-verified database (HIST-071) and Pantheon (HIST-072) cover notable people worldwide but inherit Wikipedia biases; European elite lifespans (HIST-073) cover nobles; Rulers.org (EXEC-054) lists heads of state; historical legislator data are LEG-088 to LEG-090. For the German Reichstag, LEG-092 (Best, GESIS; deputies 1867-1918 and early roll calls, access on request) is the fuller biographical source, and LEG-091 (Loesch, ICPSR 38004) pairs biographies with roll calls for 1867-1890 under ICPSR registration.

concept: City populations and demographic history
ids: HIST-074; HIST-075; HIST-076; HIST-077; HIST-024; GEO-024
how_to_choose: Reba-Reitsma-Seto (HIST-074) give the longest global city series; Buringh (HIST-075) and Bosker-Buringh-van Zanden (HIST-076) cover Europe and the Middle East 700-2000; the Human Mortality Database (HIST-077) gives mortality; African population estimates (HIST-024) and HYDE (GEO-024) give long-run population.

concept: Election returns before the modern era
ids: ELEC-150; ELEC-151; ELEC-152; ELEC-153; ELEC-154; ELEC-155; ELEC-101
how_to_choose: A New Nation Votes (ELEC-101) and Mapping Early American Elections (ELEC-155) cover 1787-1825; ICPSR studies give early returns (ELEC-150), referenda and primaries (ELEC-151) and Southern primaries (ELEC-152); the Southern Voting Project (ELEC-153) and state legislative returns (ELEC-154) cover later periods.

group: Historical text and archives as data
concept: Digitised newspapers, court records and data hubs
ids: HIST-078; HIST-079; HIST-080; HIST-081; HIST-082; HIST-083; HIST-084
how_to_choose: American Stories (HIST-078) and Newswire (HIST-079) give structured newspaper text; Newspaper Navigator (HIST-080) is discontinued; the Old Bailey Proceedings (HIST-081) give court records; CHIA, DARMC and IISH (HIST-082 to 084) host many smaller historical datasets.

concept: Money raised and spent in federal elections
how_to_choose: FEC data (AREA-010) are the official filings; DIME (AREA-011) links donors across cycles and levels and adds CFscores; OpenSecrets (AREA-014) adds industry coding but its access has tightened. Use ELEC-122 only for FEC certified results, not money.

group: U.S. state campaign finance and competition
concept: State-level money, finance law and party competition
ids: AREA-004; AREA-015; AREA-016; AREA-017; AREA-018; AREA-001; AREA-002
how_to_choose: FollowTheMoney (AREA-004) for state contributions; the CFI and Jensen-Beyle databases (AREA-015 to AREA-017) for finance law and gubernatorial spending; Ranney and Holbrook-Van Dunk measures (AREA-018) and Klarner partisan balance (AREA-001) for competition; NCSL tables (AREA-002) for current composition.

concept: Registered lobbying and foreign influence
how_to_choose: LDA filings (POLICY-081) for U.S. domestic lobbying, FARA (POLICY-082) for agents of foreign principals, LobbyView (POLICY-022) for firm identifiers and bill links, Integrity Watch EU (POLICY-085, advocacy producer) for EU meetings.

concept: Presidential documents and unilateral action
how_to_choose: The American Presidency Project (AREA-012) for documents and tables; Federal Register executive-order listings (EXEC-049) for official counts; the proclamations and Presidential Policymaking datasets (EXEC-055, EXEC-056) for coded significance; BUR-043 for appointee vacancies.

concept: Who registers and votes
how_to_choose: The CPS Voting and Registration Supplement (AREA-013) for self-reported turnout by group and state (apply a correction for over-reporting); candidate-level results in ELEC-156.

concept: Member-state voting and bargaining in the Council
how_to_choose: The official voting dataset (LEG-096) is discontinued; use SWP public voting data (LEG-097) for votes, the Negotiations in the Council dataset (LEG-098) for positions and outcomes, EMU Positions (LEG-099) for euro-area reform, and comitology votes (BUR-044) for implementing acts.

concept: Who staffs and runs the Commission
how_to_choose: Döring's Commissioners data (EXEC-057) for the College 1958-2014; PEU (BUR-046) for Commissioners, Directors-General and Secretaries-General, updated to 2025; ECIO (BUR-045) for internal units and portfolios.

group: EU law, compliance and differentiated integration
concept: EU legal acts, infringements and opt-outs
ids: CONST-100; CONST-101; POLICY-083; POLICY-084; AREA-021; INFRA-034
how_to_choose: EvoEU (CONST-100) for links among EU legal acts; EUIP (POLICY-083, 2002-2020) and the Berlin Infringement Database (POLICY-084, 1978-2019, reasoned-opinion stage onward) for compliance; EUDIFF (CONST-101) for differentiation; the eulaw API (AREA-021, unreachable on 2026-11-06) or the eurlex R package (INFRA-034) for retrieval.

concept: EU spending and harmonised European statistics
how_to_choose: Cohesion Open Data (AREA-023) for fund finances by programme and region, Kohesio (AREA-022) for individual projects and beneficiaries; Eurostat (PE-026) for harmonised statistics, AMECO (PE-167) for macro series and forecasts, the ECB portal (PE-168) for monetary and financial data, the business and consumer surveys (PE-169) for sentiment; data.europa.eu (AREA-024) only as a search layer.

concept: Official legislative data services by country
how_to_choose: Use the parliament's own API where one exists (Ireland LEG-100, Switzerland LEG-101, Korea LEG-109, Taiwan LEG-110, Israel LEG-111, Japan's Diet record TEXT-101); OpenParlData.ch (LEG-102) harmonises Swiss federal and cantonal data; biographical handbooks (LEG-094, LEG-095) for members and roles.

concept: Official and scholarly election returns by country
ids: ELEC-157; ELEC-158; ELEC-159; ELEC-160; ELEC-161; ELEC-162; ELEC-165; ELEC-166; ELEC-167; ELEC-168; ELEC-169; ELEC-170; ELEC-171; ELEC-172; ELEC-173
how_to_choose: Prefer the election authority's own archive (Italy ELEC-160, Spain ELEC-161, France ELEC-162, Korea ELEC-166, New Zealand ELEC-159); use scholarly compilations where official data are fragmentary (Japan ELEC-165, Pakistan ELEC-169, Turkey ELEC-171) and candidate-background data such as MyNeta (ELEC-168) for India. For Russia, RED (ELEC-172) harmonises federal precinct results 2000-2024 (data deposit not yet confirmed); for Taiwan, the NCCU Election Study Center database (ELEC-173) covers public-office elections from 1992.

concept: Careers of Chinese officials
how_to_choose: Jiang's database (AREA-045) for prefecture-level leaders, the CCP Elite database (AREA-046) for central Party and state posts, and the NCCU database (AREA-047) for a broader roster; check overlapping years and office definitions before merging.

concept: Official statistics portals by country
ids: AREA-026; AREA-027; AREA-031; AREA-052; AREA-060; AREA-061; AREA-062; AREA-063; AREA-064; AREA-065; AREA-066; AREA-067; AREA-068; AREA-069; AREA-070; AREA-071; AREA-072; AREA-073; INFRA-039
how_to_choose: Use the producing office's portal (and its API where one exists, e.g. e-Stat AREA-061, KOSIS AREA-062, Statistics Canada AREA-067, IBGE SIDRA AREA-068) rather than secondary copies; the UN directory (INFRA-039) lists offices not catalogued here.

group: Regional statistical portals and commercial country databases
concept: Multi-country regional statistics
ids: AREA-038; AREA-039; AREA-040; AREA-042; AREA-054; AREA-055; AREA-056; AREA-057; AREA-058; AREA-059; AREA-006; AREA-007; AREA-008; AREA-035; AREA-049; AREA-051; PE-171
how_to_choose: UN regional commission portals (Africa AREA-039, Asia-Pacific AREA-054, Arab region AREA-055, Europe AREA-056) and regional bodies (ASEAN AREA-057, Pacific AREA-058) re-publish national figures for comparison; ERF (AREA-059) and the IDB portal (AREA-042) add microdata and regional series; commercial products (AREA-006 to AREA-008, AREA-035, AREA-049, AREA-051, PE-171) add long series and translation at a cost.

concept: Comparable data on Latin American constitutions, laws and governance
how_to_choose: SIGLA (AREA-074, Georgetown) is the maintained successor to the Political Database of the Americas (AREA-041, decommissioned 2010); full data exist for only a few countries, so check coverage per table. The Statistical Abstract of Latin America (AREA-043) is a print series that ended in 2002.

concept: Who holds cabinet posts in African governments
how_to_choose: African Cabinet Politics (EXEC-058) records ministers and portfolios; ECAG (IDENT-137) codes the ethnic composition of the same governments, so the two can be linked. Global cabinet datasets such as WhoGov (EXEC-004) cover Africa with fewer variables.

concept: Codes for countries and areas
how_to_choose: ISO 3166 (INFRA-040) for current countries in official statistics; UN M49 (INFRA-041) adds numeric codes and regional groupings; World Bank groups (INFRA-042) for income and lending categories; COW (IR-006) and Gleditsch-Ward (IR-016) lists for state-system panels with entry and exit dates.

concept: Converting names and codes between schemes
ids: INFRA-022; INFRA-051; INFRA-052; INFRA-053; INFRA-054; INFRA-055; INFRA-023; INFRA-024
how_to_choose: countrycode (INFRA-022) in R and country_converter (INFRA-051) in Python are the general tools; kountry (INFRA-052) for Stata; ISOcodes and pycountry (INFRA-053, INFRA-054) supply ISO tables only; use democracyData's year-aware coder (INFRA-023) or states (INFRA-024) when membership changes over time.

concept: Linking U.S. states, counties and agencies
how_to_choose: ANSI/FIPS (INFRA-044) is the official standard; use the ICPSR codes (INFRA-045) for older ICPSR and Voteview files, the NBER SSA-FIPS crosswalk (INFRA-046) for Social Security and Medicare data, and LEAIC (INFRA-047) to link police agencies to places.

concept: Crosswalks between industry, trade and occupation codes
how_to_choose: Pierce-Schott (INFRA-048) for U.S. trade-to-industry links; the concordance R package (INFRA-056) bundles several trade and industry concordances; ISCO-08 (INFRA-049) and the UNSD registry (INFRA-050) for official occupation and economic classifications.

concept: Ready-merged or package-built panels
ids: INFRA-021; INFRA-023; INFRA-001; INFRA-019; INFRA-057; REG-057
how_to_choose: peacesciencer (INFRA-021) for peace-science panels, democracyData (INFRA-023) for regime measures, Demscore (INFRA-001) and QoG (REG-057) for merged country-year files, the IPE Data Resource (INFRA-019) for political economy; retroharmonize (INFRA-057) for harmonising survey waves yourself.

concept: Programmatic access to official statistics
how_to_choose: Use SDMX clients (INFRA-062) or the World Bank clients (INFRA-064) to query producers directly; DBnomics (INFRA-061) offers one API over about 94 providers but is a mirror; EconDataverse (INFRA-063) wraps several international sources in tidy R packages; Google Data Commons (INFRA-065) links many public sources in one graph.

concept: Where to deposit and find open research data
ids: INFRA-067; INFRA-069; INFRA-070; INFRA-071; INFRA-072; INFRA-073; INFRA-074
how_to_choose: Harvard Dataverse (INFRA-067) is the political-science default and hosts most journal collections; Zenodo (INFRA-069) is free, CERN-backed and links to GitHub; figshare (INFRA-071), Dryad (INFRA-072) and Mendeley Data (INFRA-073) are less used in the field; OSF (INFRA-070) is ending new projects; Code Ocean (INFRA-074) packages runnable code.

concept: National archives with curation and preservation
ids: INFRA-005; INFRA-002; INFRA-004; INFRA-075; INFRA-077; INFRA-078; INFRA-083; INFRA-084; INFRA-085; INFRA-088; INFRA-089
how_to_choose: Use the archive of the country whose data you study, or ICPSR (INFRA-005), GESIS (INFRA-002) and the UK Data Service (INFRA-004) for large international holdings; CESSDA (INFRA-003) searches the European archives together; Borealis (INFRA-088) and ADA (INFRA-089) serve Canada and Australia.

concept: Journal replication files
how_to_choose: Harvard Dataverse collections for IR journals (INFRA-026) and twenty other political-science journals (INFRA-091); the JPR archive at PRIO (INFRA-092); QDR (INFRA-093) for qualitative and multi-method material.

concept: Copies of U.S. government data removed or at risk
ids: INFRA-096; INFRA-097; INFRA-098; INFRA-099; INFRA-100; INFRA-101
how_to_choose: DataLumos (INFRA-096) and the Harvard LIL Data.gov Archive (INFRA-098) hold the largest documented copies; the Data Rescue Project (INFRA-097) tracks what has been saved where; Data-PASS (INFRA-101) coordinates archives; the UChicago and UCSB mirrors (INFRA-099, INFRA-100) are smaller. Check each copy against any restored official version.

concept: Finding datasets and their uses
ids: INFRA-102; INFRA-103; INFRA-104; INFRA-106; INFRA-107; INFRA-058; INFRA-108; INFRA-109
how_to_choose: Google Dataset Search (INFRA-102) and DataCite Commons (INFRA-104) find datasets; re3data (INFRA-103) finds repositories; the ICPSR Bibliography (INFRA-106) and Data Citation Index (INFRA-107, commercial) find publications using data; PolData (INFRA-058) lists political datasets; DataPortals.org and Open Data Inception (INFRA-108, INFRA-109) list open government portals.
